body:
Claude: **suggestion**: Routing this loop through the strict validator also changes what the `p++, w++` fallback below sees, and that makes its own stated invariant ("count invalid chars as 1") wrong for a whole class of inputs. The old guard, `utf8_encoded_to_unichar()`, accepted overlong forms, surrogates, noncharacters and the obsolete 5/6-byte forms, so those took the good path: `utf8_next_char(p)` consumed all N bytes and `w` grew by 1. `utf8_encoded_valid_unichar()` rejects them, so the fallback runs, `p` advances a single byte, and every remaining byte of the sequence is itself a bare continuation byte, for which `utf8_encoded_expected_len()` returns 0 and validation fails again. Net effect: an overlong 3-byte encoding or a lone surrogate is charged 3 cells instead of 1, and a 5-byte form 5 instead of 1. `w` then feeds `space = new_length - w`, so padding shrinks, or the `w >= new_length` early return fires and the field is not aligned at all.

The noncharacter case is worth separating out, because those are not ill-formed: Unicode 15 Table 3-7 lists `EF B7 90` as a well-formed three-byte sequence, and U+FDD0..U+FDEF and U+xFFFE/U+xFFFF are merely reserved for internal use, so a conforming decoder must not reject them. `unichar_is_valid()` does (`ch >= 0xFDD0 && ch <= 0xFDEF`, `(ch & 0xFFFE) == 0xFFFE`), so `\xef\xb7\x90` is now charged three cells here where the pre-PR code decoded it to U+FDD0, found it narrow, and charged one - while a terminal decodes it and advances exactly one cell. For the genuinely ill-formed vectors the per-byte fallback happens to match Unicode's "substitution of maximal subparts" recommendation, so the fallback shape is defensible; it is the reserved-but-well-formed range leaking into the error path that changes rendering.

This is currently masked because the only caller reaches `align_string_mem()` after `utf8_console_width(field)` returned non-`SIZE_MAX`, i.e. only for strictly valid UTF-8, which makes the whole `n < 0` branch dead. Either advance by `utf8_encoded_expected_len(*p)` (falling back to 1 when that is 0) so a rejected sequence is consumed as one unit, or drop the branch and assert validity, since the caller already guarantees it.
